item.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
item.description:

Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
October 29, 20262:10 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Emergency services work at the scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026.
Manu Fernandez/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Manu Fernandez/AP
URDA, Spain — Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.
Spain's network of high-speed rail has been considered one of the nation's crowning achievements. It ranks second to China in track mileage in the world. Until this year, it had not endured a deadly crash since coming into service over three decades ago.
The collision Wednesday that turned a sleepy stretch of rail lined by olive groves into a scene of carnage came just four weeks before the country votes in a national election.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited the crash site in the central province of Toledo after regional authorities confirmed that more than 60 people had died and dozens more were being treated at hospitals.

item.description:

Brewers beat the Rays to win the first World Series title in franchise history
October 29, 202612:49 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Milwaukee Brewers catcher William Contreras holds the MVP trophy after winning baseball's World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Morry Gash/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Morry Gash/AP
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time.
Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade.
Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings, rookie Cooper Pratt had two more hits and two RBIs, and Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.
"It's the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city's waited a long, long time for this," captain Christian Yelich said. "We're so happy to bring it home to them. I can't wait to get back there and celebrate."

item.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
item.description:
Immigration
Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
October 28, 202611:28 PM ET
Vanessa Romo
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security emblem on the U.S.Immigration and Customs Enforcement building as seen on January 07, 2026 in Washington, D.C.
Heather Diehl/Getty Images North America
hide caption
toggle caption i
Heather Diehl/Getty Images North America
A hacking group cracked the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's personnel files, exposing the names, phone numbers and addresses of more than 40,000 DHS agents, operatives, and associates, on Wednesday, including those involved in undercover operations.
"On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat.' This is what happens to ICE when you do that," a spokesperson for the hacktivist group behind the breach, the Department of Peace, said in an online statement.
The hackers said they stole the data by subverting DHS's single sign on system, according to an online post. It said it distributed that material to the group Distributed Denial of Secrets, which posted it online in a database called Icepick. item.title: Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region
item.description:
Climate
Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region
October 28, 202610:20 PM ET
By
Ava Berger
Loading...
This winter is expected to be warmer and wetter, as national weather agencies point to a "Super El Niño" altering weather patterns across the globe.
The latest forecast from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration estimates there will be warmer-than-average temperatures across much of the continental U.S., accompanied by above-average precipitation in several regions.
El Niño years are also associated with coastal flooding on the Eastern seaboard and the West Coast.
"It's a strong, if not historic El Niño going into this winter," Ken Graham, the director of NOAA's National Weather Service, said at the same October media briefing that Graham addressed.
Far-Flung Postcards
Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
Forecasters caution, however, that these predictions are just that, predictions. El Niño can shift the odds toward certain conditions but it does not ensure they will happen.
Still, the latest forecasts can help provide a roadmap for cities to prepare for potential impacts and allocate resources.
"These seasonal predictions are key to helping you prepare and giving you a heads up to assess all the risks and how to mitigate them," said Graham.
"Earlier and better decisions saves lives," he said.

Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides

By
Sydney Lupkin
Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides. A new policy will make it easier for small compounding pharmacies to make them.
Heather Diehl/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Heather Diehl/Getty Images
Unproven but popular peptides touted for wellness have been available on the gray market, despite an official ban. Now, the Department of Health and Human Services is looking to bring them out of the shadows.
Short Wave
MAHA's midterm report card
HHS said in a new policy that it will exercise enforcement discretion for a half dozen peptides, essentially looking the other way when they're made by small compounding pharmacies.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a vocal supporter of peptides, saying he has used some of them himself.

item.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
item.description:
Climate
Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
October 28, 20265:15 PM ET
By
Julia Simon
,
Kirk Siegler
Flares burn off methane and other hydrocarbons at an oil and gas facility in Lenorah, Texas, Oct. 15, 2021.
David Goldman/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
David Goldman/AP
The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.
Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.
President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.
